title: Finite coefficient extension and common-stage descent of restriction maps
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0=\mathbf F_q,k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For a scheme $W$, write $R_W=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$ on the small pro-etale site $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the strict derived reductions $K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_W}(A_n)_W$, and exact restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_n$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Let $Rf_*$ be the tower direct image of [def-weil-derived-direct-image].

For a geometric point $y:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point], set $S=X\times_Ys$ with projections $v:S\to X$, $h:S\to s$ [def-pc-base-change], and $P_y=\{x:s\to X\mid fx=y\}$. For $x\in P_y$ let $i_x:s\to S$ be the unique lift, so $vi_x=x$ and $hi_x=\operatorname{id}_s$. This is a finite set; an empty sum indexed by $P_y$ is the zero object. Write $L(-)^*$ for the completed integral pullback of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and $(-)_n^*$ for its exact finite-coefficient inverse image.

Choose an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ containing $E$. For any finite coefficient extension $E\subset L\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], let $C_{L/E,W}$ denote integral derived change of completed coefficient rings and $T_{L/E,W}$ its raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Integral ordinary ringed-topos direct image agrees with the reduction-tower direct image through the projection-normalized comparison. There are coherent natural isomorphisms
$$C_{L/E,Y}Rf_{*,E}\simeq Rf_{*,L}C_{L/E,X},\quad
C_{L/E,W'}Lg_E^*\simeq Lg_L^*C_{L/E,W}$$
for $g\in\{y,v,h,x,i_x\}$ with its indicated source $W'$ and target $W$, whenever the displayed pullback is used. These preserve the integral constructible categories. After rationalization they compare the prescribed rational functors; exact point sections have the compatible scalar comparison [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point].

Under these comparisons, scalar extension carries the integral finite-fibre exchange $Ly^*Rf_*K\to Rh_*Lv^*K$ and the counit restriction $Rh_*Lv^*K\to\bigoplus_{x\in P_y}Lx^*K$ to those at $L$. The same is true after rationalization and point sections. This specifies the actual arrows: on coefficient-level tensor representatives the $x$-component sends $a\otimes m$ to $a\otimes(m|_{i_x})$ and the exchange map is the scalar-extended counit mate. The comparisons respect identities and composition of coefficient extensions, including ramified ones; no common quotient exponent between two different uniformizers is assumed.

Consequently the functors, both restriction maps, and all identities between them descend independently of a chosen finite field of definition to the common-stage category $D^b_c(-,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Every finite collection of objects, morphisms, triangles and equations is represented after enlarging to one finite stage. A stagewise t-exact direct image and its exact heart restriction retain these properties for the common-stage standard pair [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure].

proof.text: Apply finitePoints to the finite geometric fibre. Apply the integral assembly lemma to obtain G,I,N,J with all integral, scalar, arrow, tower normalizations and TensorRestrictionFormula.
Apply rational assembly to G,I and their normalized/coherent laws. It supplies R, normalized direct-image descent and conditional exact-heart descent.

For point sections form psi = the sections-tensor map followed by sections of the completion comparison. Naturality of psi on each integral arrow, conjugated by its component inverses, is exactly integral SectionsCompatible. Rational SectionsCompatible is naturality of the already specified pointRationalFibreScalarIso.

Choose one eventual representative for each of finitely many arrows, a finite-stage distinguished triangle for each distinguished triangle, and one eventual-equality witness for each equation. Directedness gives a single upper bound for these stages and every object stage. Transport all representatives there; use isoToStage for the object and arrow squares, transIso and mapTriangleCompIso for triangles, and naturality of the associator to transport equality witnesses. Finite.exists_le includes empty index types, so the empty collection is also covered.

For TExactDescent, write a common-stage half-object as an isomorphic included finite-stage object. Apply the stagewise preservation hypothesis. Map its representing isomorphism and compose with Morphism.ιCompFunctorIso; this represents the image in the same half. Combine this with all preceding conjuncts.
